morphology: A tightly recurved early coil grows into a greatly expanded irregular final whorl, cap-like rather than tower-shaped. Overall body squat and rounded, with small rolled apex at one end and broad aperture opposite.

Large asymmetric oval aperture has a distinctly uneven rim and bends in its outline. Show retained rim and a modest inset mineral-filled opening, not a perfect circular tube end or a solid shell with no mouth boundary.

The upper surface rises and bends away from the early coil. Broad lobes and directional growth undulations converge toward the small apex. Avoid radial symmetric limpet geometry or a flat ammonite disk.

Fossil aperture is substantially mineral-filled and chipped. Preserve a restrained shallow recess under surviving lip; do not invent an empty deep funnel. Do not reproduce paper whitening/label patches or museum text.

Few broad collabral growth undulations suffice. No spines, strong spiral keels, shell chambers, cowry teeth or soft parts. Rounded low-poly facets, matte neutral stone, no pedestal or attached crinoid.
uncertainty: Selected specimen is mineral-filled, not an open pristine living shell. Thin lost lip and internal lumen unknown; no invented internal depth.
Fine apex/protoconch details below model scale may be simplified. Do not enlarge tiny larval features for decoration.
Five reference views constrain exterior; small damaged regions may be smoothed conservatively but no idealized symmetry. Colour is artistic stone, photographs are grayscale.
palette: Matte neutral grey/tan shell; slightly darker subdued mineral fill, no white label patch.
acceptance_focus: Front: expanded uneven aperture and preserved lip remain readable despite mineral fill. No sealed undifferentiated blob or invented deep empty cone.
Side: recurved early coil and bulging cap are coherent, not a stack of whorls or flat disk.
Top: small off-centre coil transitions continuously into expanded, irregular final whorl.
Perspective: connected lip/body/filled recess; retain asymmetry without excessive broken debris.
Produce4actual renders, geometry tests, pinned local dependencies and two isolated deterministic rebuilds. Prep is not scientific/modelPASS.
